name: Projected Distinguishing Range
definition: The **projected distinguishing range** of $\mathcal H$ is $$\mathrm R^p(\mathcal H)=\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal X}\mathrm R(\mathcal H_{|S}),$$ where $\mathrm R$ is distinguishing range. Thus it is the largest, over coordinate projections, of the fewest coordinates that distinguish every pair of projected concepts.
graph_summary: Largest distinguishing range attained by a coordinate projection.
description: The projection-monotone closure of distinguishing range, introduced in this catalogue.

monotonic.proof: For every coordinate set S, a subfamily projection is a subfamily of the corresponding original projection, and distinguishing range cannot increase under taking a subfamily. Taking the maximum over S preserves this inequality.

p_monotonic.proof: Every projection of a projection is a projection of the original class. The defining maximum for the projected distinguishing range of a projection is therefore taken over a subset of the projections of the original class.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a coordinate projection, so it follows from the preceding monotonicity properties.

doubly_monotonic.proof: It is monotonic both under subfamilies and under coordinate projections by the preceding arguments.
